before: CodexBar is a health and quota signal, not a complete model inventory.

Cursor auto is a harness choice, never a model identity for formal review. Operator decision 2026-09-30 (#9274): Auto runs only a well-defined coding task (a write-capable dispatch typed --research-role implementation, with owned paths and a green DoR issue card); every other Cursor use pins a concrete approved model (orchestrator_seats.cursor).

GPT-6 routes are native Codex only until Cursor exposes a verified GPT-6 slug. Claude Opus 5.5 reviews and drives through native Claude only; no Claude model reviews through Cursor (operator decision D-129, #10464). Grok is native CLI ONLY at grok-4.7 for every seat (interactive, orchestrator, ask, dispatch), with the Cursor transport fallback. Operator decision 2026-10-05 (#9769): native Grok and the Cursor seat pinned to grok-4.7-high are regular code/infra reviewers at every risk, including critical; verdicts require runtime model attestation and exclude xAI-authored changes. Operator order 2026-09-22 (#8464) rotates from grok-4.6; #6865 previously retired opencode first-party xai/grok-* for orchestrator seats — opencode remains unsanctioned for grok. Hermes and OpenRouter grok routes remain banned. grok-4.6 and grok-4.7-build-fast are not admitted.

Kimi K3 workers (`kimi`, `kimicc`, and catalog ids `kimi-code/k3*`) use the native `kimi` CLI subscription path only (`catalog_transport` / `transports`: `native_kimi`). OpenRouter is forbidden as a Kimi worker bus. Do not relaunch OpenRouter-for-subscribed-models patterns for Moonshot/Kimi K3. OpenRouter remains mainly Pool + Gemma access.

Kimi: web, UI and backend coding only — no Ukrainian-language content, no reviews, consults, design or rules. Kimi seats (`kimi`, `kimicc`, every `kimi-code/*` / `kimi-k3*` id) take workspace-write implementation of the allowlisted UI and backend paths (KIMI_OWNED_ROOTS) only; they carry no review, consult, advisor, or ACP-discussion role and are absent from review_candidates and review_ladders; dispatch, the runtime, ACP and the fleet-comms authority refuse everything else before any side effect (scripts/agent_runtime/kimi_admission.py).

EXEMPT (not a fleet seat) — scripts/projects/open_model_data Phase 3 v2.1 ROLE_EXECUTION still pins harness opencode + exact_model grok-4.5 for ukrainian_source_reviewer / cross_family_code_infra_reviewer / textbook_nonhit_auditor (and OPENCODE_REVIEW_MODEL xai/grok-4.5). Those pins live in hash-bound v2.1 evidence/validator artifacts (phase3_functional_roles.py validator_sha256 + phase3_source_production_transport.py inventory sha); rotating or rewriting them is outside the fleet seat list and requires a separate open-model-data rebind (#6870 item 3). The same rebind must cover gemini-3.6/3.7 (including Flash variants), claude-fable-5 and grok-4.6 pins in those hash-bound Phase 3 artifacts. Fleet routing must not read them.
Composer 2.5 derives from Kimi 2.5; native Kimi K3 diverged. Composer 2.5 conservatively shares Moonshot independence lineage with Kimi.

approval_contract.before:
(binding) — new decisions only.** Agents must **not**
    invent or unilaterally adopt **new** architecture, local layout, process, or policy
    without **present-tense approval** from the **operator** or **designated approval**: two
    frontier families agree through the designated advisors, **Opus 5.5** (`claude-opus-5-5`)
    and **Sol 6.1** (`gpt-6.1-sol`). When one of them authored the proposal, the other's
    approval completes it; a proposal by any other agent (Gemini, Grok, Kimi or another seat)
    needs both; if they disagree, the operator decides (#9583, #9616; roster may change — confirm via `/api/rules` / `model-assignment.md` when unsure;
    do not treat stale digests as roster). Fable and the former Astra seat hold no advisory,
    approval or review role.
    **Kimi: web, UI and backend coding only — no Ukrainian-language content, no reviews,
    consults, design or rules.** Discussion/panels improve quality but do **not** replace advisor approval
    for design. This gate governs *deciding*, not *implementing*: once the operator or an
    advisor has ordered or approved the work, item 10 governs — drive it to a complete outcome
    without re-opening a GO request. Routine implementation of already-queued work does not
    need a new advisor turn. Slicing an already-approved user-visible outcome into PR-sized
    stages is item-10 disobedience, not an extra exemption from this gate; unrelated outcomes
    stay in other PRs.
    Violations: shipping
    helpers/layouts/process "for now", redefining primary-checkout semantics, flipping gates
    without an advisor record, or citing this gate to pause already-decided implementation.
